source.title: Disentangling Neuron Representations with Concept Vectors
source.authors: Laura O'Mahony; V. Andrearczyk; H. Muller; Mara Graziani

record.tranche_reason: Tests visual neuron polysemanticity using a different method: clusters of activation-space embeddings for top-activating images, rather than relying only on individual neurons’ maximally activating images.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior examples and superposition accounts, but those citations are not this study’s results. Its own results include neuron examples, an aggregate statement about analyzed neurons, clustering-threshold effects, concept-vector comparisons, and human evaluations.
record.test_reason: Mainly a methods paper for splitting polysemantic neurons into concept vectors. Its own analysis of Inception V3 Mixed 7b still reports specific polysemantic neurons with unrelated top-activating groups (apples/sports, peacocks/vans, toilet paper/dog faces). It also states that most analysed neurons showed some polysemanticity. This bears on V1 in a new vision model, and the dmax dendrograms bear on V7. Method-performance results (concept vector vs neuron direction, human ratings of concepts) do not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that polysemantic neurons can be disentangled into concept vectors (linear combinations of neurons) that are coherent and human-understandable, and that latent representations are much more similar to these vectors than to neuron directions. They note dependence on the data used for clustering and that all experiments use image data, as a proof of concept.
record.recipe_differences: Uses top-activating examples as a starting point, but clusters their pooled activation embeddings and forms concept vectors from cluster means; it is not a reproduction of the cited original neuron-analysis method.
record.method_sensitivity: The clustering distance threshold dmax changes concept granularity and can merge or split clusters.

fits_no_version.finding: Projections and cosine similarities of top-projecting activations are much higher for the derived concept vectors than for the neuron direction. Human raters found the concepts coherent (100% intruder accuracy) and agreed with the labels 97% of the time.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polysemantic neurons can be decomposed into activation-space directions that are more monosemantic than the neuron basis.

record.peer_reviewed: 2023 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
record.problems: Exploratory proof of concept using an undersampled ImageNet subset (130 random images per class), one architecture and the default Mixed 7b layer; the authors give no denominator for the neurons behind the majority-polysemanticity statement. Human evaluation used n = 8 participants. The authors also note dependence on the data used to generate clusters.

untested.parts: InceptionV1 and the cat-face/car-front example; only Inception V3 Mixed 7b is studied.
Superposition is offered only as a cited or speculative explanation; no capacity test.
All; one architecture and one layer.
How common shared-feature versus unrelated mixtures are; only a handful of hand-picked neurons, judged qualitatively.
Activation-range slices (only the top 100 activations are used) and explanation-scoring methods.

missing.what: For neuron 35, inter-cluster distances (apple vs sport images) are considerably higher than intra-cluster distances, and the two concept vectors differ across other dimensions. This is evidence that the two groups are genuinely distinct in activation space rather than one shared feature.
missing.locator: Results, Fig. 4(b); Appendix A.2, Fig. A.9

missing.what: The minimum cluster size of 5 removed neuron 35's net-like third group, a measurement choice that changes how many concepts are counted.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a method paper. Claim-relevant evidence is limited to qualitative neuron examples and an undenominated 'majority' statement. The neurons are numbered low (1, 5, 13, 16, 27, 35), which suggests only the first few dozen neurons were examined. V6 verdicts rest on qualitative cluster separation; the clustering tool is designed to split groups, which weakens the challenge.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test InceptionV1 specifically or the cited cat-face/car-front example; it studies Inception V3.
No transformer language models or language neuron measurements.
Discusses superposition as a possible account but does not test whether capacity pressure causes the reported polysemanticity.
Does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes, or whether there is sufficient capacity.
Uses one architecture and layer; does not compare activation functions, architectures, or regularization, or measure performance costs.
Tests selected Inception V3 neurons qualitatively, not how common shared-feature explanations are across models or neurons.
Tests sensitivity to clustering distance threshold, but not alternative activation-range slices or explanation-scoring methods.

rows.subject: Inception V3 (IV3), neuron 35, Mixed 7b
rows.operation_detail: Clustered activation-space embeddings of the top-activating images and inspected the resulting clusters.
rows.measure: The neuron activated highly for apples, sports, and three net-like images; clustering resulted in 3 clusters, with the net-like cluster removed because it had fewer than 5 images. The remaining images formed apple and sports clusters; Fig. 4 reports 52 images remaining after step 3.
rows.value: 3 clusters before removal; apple and sports clusters retained after removal
rows.note: The authors describe apples and sports as distinct concepts; the small net-like cluster was excluded by the stated minimum cluster size.
rows.check: Observed for V1. For V6 the finding runs the opposite way: clustering in activation space separates apples and sports into distinct directions rather than revealing one shared feature. It should count as reversed for V6, and the evidence is qualitative.

source_check.locator_found: Results, neuron 35 paragraph (3 clusters at dmax 15; net-like cluster removed, <5 images); Fig. 2a

rows.subject: Inception V3 (IV3), neuron 16, Mixed 7b
rows.operation_detail: Applied the same top-activating-image clustering procedure.
rows.measure: The neuron activated for categories of elliptical shapes; the procedure yielded one cluster and one concept vector.
rows.note: The paper presents this as a monosemantic comparison, not as evidence against the claim that some neurons are polysemantic.
rows.check: Monosemantic comparator. It does not count against V1, which claims only that some neurons are polysemantic.

rows.subject: Inception V3 (IV3), neuron 1, Mixed 7b
rows.operation_detail: Clustered embeddings of top-activating images to separate concepts.
rows.measure: The neuron activated for underwater images; inspection distinguished general underwater scenes from scuba-diver images, and the method yielded two clusters/concept vectors.
rows.value: two clusters: general underwater scenes and scuba divers
rows.note: The authors describe these as related directions that can nevertheless be differentiated.
rows.check: The authors say the underwater and scuba-diver groups are 'not entirely conceptually different'. That is not the unrelated-input mixture V1 names, so it is partial for V1. For V6 it is consistent with related facets of one job; the state should be read per version.

rows.subject: Inception V3 (IV3), neuron 35, Mixed 7b
rows.operation_detail: Varied the agglomerative-clustering distance threshold used to set cluster granularity.
rows.measure: The dendrogram indicates 2 clusters at thresholds around 16–28; thresholds below 16 produce more clusters.
rows.value: 2 clusters around dmax 16–28; more clusters below 16
rows.note: The number of discovered concepts depends on the selected clustering threshold.
rows.check: The threshold changes neuron 35's cluster count (3 vs 2), but the neuron stays polysemantic at every threshold reported. Polysemantic status itself does not flip, so this is partial for V7.

rows.subject: Inception V3 (IV3), neuron 1, Mixed 7b
rows.operation_detail: Varied the agglomerative-clustering distance threshold for the neuron’s activation embeddings.
rows.measure: The dendrogram gives two clusters around thresholds 14–17.
rows.note: The paper says a higher threshold above 17 yields one cluster; that outcome is recorded separately in r6.

rows.subject: Inception V3 (IV3), neuron 1, Mixed 7b
rows.operation_detail: Varied the agglomerative-clustering distance threshold for the neuron’s activation embeddings.
rows.measure: The dendrogram gives one cluster above threshold 17.
rows.note: Changing the threshold merges the two more fine-grained clusters.

rows.measure: The authors report that the majority of neurons they analyzed showed some amount of polysemanticity.

rows.note: No denominator or detailed neuron-by-neuron tally is given.
rows.check: 'Some amount of polysemanticity' has no denominator. It does not say whether the mixtures are unrelated or facet-like, so it does not bear on V6. Remove the V6 link.

rows.subject: Inception V3 (IV3), neuron 5, Mixed 7b
rows.operation_detail: Clustered and inspected top-activating image embeddings for a polysemantic neuron.

rows.note: The paper gives this as an additional polysemantic-neuron example.
rows.check: Observed for V1. For V6 it is effectively reversed, since peacocks and vans split into two distinct vectors. The evidence is qualitative.

statements.correction: The study tests Inception V3 (Mixed 7b), a later Inception variant, not InceptionV1. InceptionV1/GoogLeNet itself is examined in arXiv:2211.12312, arXiv:2406.03662 and arXiv:1711.05611. Call it 'an Inception V3 test of V1', or limit the comparison explicitly to the list.
statements.problem: All numbers and neuron descriptions match the text. But 'the nearest Inception-family test of V1' overstates: the study uses Inception V3, not InceptionV1, and other catalog studies examine InceptionV1/GoogLeNet itself. 'The only list study with a V7 limits verdict' cannot be checked from this study.
